title: session-load --live with a window shorter than one ps listing divides by zero and writes no live row
goal: bench_load.live_rows gives per-minute figures over at least one listing's time (or refuses a window under one listing with exit 2), so a short --window never raises ZeroDivisionError

gates.question: How does live_rows treat a --window shorter than one ps listing's pause, which lists once and leaves zero elapsed seconds?
options: divide per-minute figures by at least one LIVE_TICK_S and write the rows
gates.recommendation: divide per-minute figures by at least one LIVE_TICK_S and write the rows
gates.reason: a short window still measures the one listing, and the refusal would need the CLI file, outside the touches
gates.answer: divide per-minute figures by at least one LIVE_TICK_S and write the rows

notes: Review gap 4 of SP-wv3ob5vy: bench_load.py:830 divides by elapsed/60; benchmarks.py accepts any --window above 0.
